  Steps: 1) No global exception filter is registered anywhere in server/src (confirmed via code search: only ValidationPipe's exceptionFactory handles 400s; NotFoundException/ServiceUnavailableException are plain HttpExceptions that Nest formats correctly). 2) For any other error thrown out of CatalogService (server/src/catalog/catalog.service.ts) or HealthService when prisma.*.findMany/count/findUnique/$queryRawUnsafe rejects with a generic Error (e.g. a dropped DB connection), Nest's built-in exception handling falls back to `{ statusCode: 500, message: 'Internal server error' }` with no 'error' property, because that fallback only applies to non-HttpException instances. 3) Reproduce deterministically with server/test/m2-error-shape.e2e-spec.ts, which overrides PrismaService with a stub whose methods reject with a generic Error, then calls GET /api/v1/categories, GET /api/v1/products, and GET /api/v1/products/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000; the assertions on res.body.error fail for all three.

Product brief:
# Product brief: ShopEase — Release 2 (Mobile Shopping App)

ShopEase is our mobile storefront for a growing retail business. Release 1 gave shoppers a working catalog and API-backed product data (guest browse). Release 2 turns that into a credible, client-demo-ready shopping experience: accounts, a proper home page, search and filters, wishlist, full checkout with mock payment, order history and tracking, coupons, and in-app support—while staying demo-safe (no live payment keys, no production push). We want customers to discover products, save favorites, check out smoothly, and come back to see their orders—without needing a full admin back office in this pass.

## Target users
- Guest shoppers who browse and add to cart without signing up (must remain supported)
- Registered customers who want saved carts or order history, faster repeat purchases, and order tracking
- Repeat buyers who use wishlists and promo codes
- Prospective retail partners or investors viewing a polished demo on Android emulator
- Our support team (indirectly)—customers reach us through a clear in-app contact channel instead of hunting for email/phone

## Business goals
- Increase conversion by offering a complete checkout path (address, review, confirmation, order number) even with mock payment
- Build trust and repeat visits through accounts, order history, and visible order status (processing → shipped → delivered)
- Improve discovery and average order value via home merchandising (banners, featured, new arrivals, categories), search, sort, and filters
- Capture intent early with wishlist so we can remarket later (local or API-backed is fine for demo)
- Run promotions at checkout with coupon codes validated against our seeded promos to prove discount workflows
- Keep engineering cost controlled: extend existing NestJS + Prisma and Flutter codebase; no full admin panel or real payment processor in this release
- Meet quality bar for demos and handoff: Flutter runs on Android emulator, analyze/tests green, server tests for new endpoints, PRD backlog updated, minimum one QA round

## Key features
- Accounts (FR-01 lite): register, log in, log out; secure token storage; optional password reset stub
- Guest + signed-in (FR-02): keep guest browse/cart; signed-in users persist cart or order history in session/API as feasible
- Home (FR-03): home route with banners, featured products, new arrivals, category entry—not only a flat product list
- Search & filters (FR-05–FR-08): keyword search; sort by price and newest; extend filters (price, category) with brand and availability where seed data supports it
- Wishlist (FR-12): save and remove favorites (local or API-backed)
- Checkout flow (FR-13–FR-15): contact + shipping address + order review; place order with confirmation screen and order number; mock payment / PaymentIntent stub acceptable
- Order history & tracking (FR-16–FR-17): list past orders; show status progression processing → shipped → delivered
- Promotions (FR-19): apply coupon code at checkout; validate against seed promos
- Support (FR-20): in-app contact/support screen with a clear contact channel
- Backend: extend NestJS OpenAPI + Prisma only as needed for orders, auth slice, coupons; keep analyze/tests green
- Baseline from prior milestones: M1 guest catalog and M2 API integration remain the foundation for Release 2 work

## Constraints
- Continue on the existing codebase—Release 2 is expansion, not a greenfield rewrite
- Demo-safe only: mock payment gateway; no real payment processor keys
- Flutter app must run on Android emulator (not a counter template app)
- flutter analyze and flutter test must pass; server tests must pass for new endpoints
- Update docs/PRD backlog section to reflect Release 2 scope; at least one QA round
- Out of scope: full admin panel (AR-01–AR-09)—document as follow-up unless time allows minimal read-only admin API
- Out of scope: production push notifications (FR-18)—log/mock only
- Out of scope: real payment processor integration

## Open questions
- Brand and store identity: official app display name, logo, primary colors, and tone of home banners—are we one vertical (e.g. general merchandise) or multi-category as seed data implies?
- Markets and compliance: which countries we ship to in the demo, currency display, and whether we need tax/VAT lines on order review for realism
- Account policy: email-only registration or phone/social login later; minimum password rules; whether guest checkout must remain after Release 2 or accounts become strongly encouraged
- Cart persistence rules: when a guest logs in, do we merge carts, replace, or ask the shopper; how long carts live on server vs device
- Wishlist: must it sync across devices for signed-in users in this release, or is device-local acceptable for demo
- Shipping: flat-rate vs tiered by order value; do we show estimated delivery dates on tracking or status labels only
- Coupons: stackable with other promos or one code per order; exclusions (sale items, categories); max discount cap
- Order tracking: carrier name and tracking number in UI or internal status only for demo
- Support channel: single channel (email form) vs phone/chat hours; SLA we promise in copy
- Password reset stub: email actually sent in demo environment or UI-only flow with message that email would be sent
- Home content: who supplies banner copy and featured product rules—manual seed, algorithm (newest), or merchandising flags in database
- Minimal read-only admin API: if attempted under time pressure, which read-only views matter most (orders list, coupon usage)
- Push notifications (FR-18 mock): which events should be logged (order shipped, back in stock) for future production scope documentation

Product brief:
# Product brief: ShopEase — Release 2 (Mobile Shopping App)

ShopEase is our mobile storefront for a growing retail business. Release 1 gave shoppers a working catalog and API-backed product data (guest browse). Release 2 turns that into a credible, client-demo-ready shopping experience: accounts, a proper home page, search and filters, wishlist, full checkout with mock payment, order history and tracking, coupons, and in-app support—while staying demo-safe (no live payment keys, no production push). We want customers to discover products, save favorites, check out smoothly, and come back to see their orders—without needing a full admin back office in this pass.

## Target users
- Guest shoppers who browse and add to cart without signing up (must remain supported)
- Registered customers who want saved carts or order history, faster repeat purchases, and order tracking
- Repeat buyers who use wishlists and promo codes
- Prospective retail partners or investors viewing a polished demo on Android emulator
- Our support team (indirectly)—customers reach us through a clear in-app contact channel instead of hunting for email/phone

## Business goals
- Increase conversion by offering a complete checkout path (address, review, confirmation, order number) even with mock payment
- Build trust and repeat visits through accounts, order history, and visible order status (processing → shipped → delivered)
- Improve discovery and average order value via home merchandising (banners, featured, new arrivals, categories), search, sort, and filters
- Capture intent early with wishlist so we can remarket later (local or API-backed is fine for demo)
- Run promotions at checkout with coupon codes validated against our seeded promos to prove discount workflows
- Keep engineering cost controlled: extend existing NestJS + Prisma and Flutter codebase; no full admin panel or real payment processor in this release
- Meet quality bar for demos and handoff: Flutter runs on Android emulator, analyze/tests green, server tests for new endpoints, PRD backlog updated, minimum one QA round

## Key features
- Accounts (FR-01 lite): register, log in, log out; secure token storage; optional password reset stub
- Guest + signed-in (FR-02): keep guest browse/cart; signed-in users persist cart or order history in session/API as feasible
- Home (FR-03): home route with banners, featured products, new arrivals, category entry—not only a flat product list
- Search & filters (FR-05–FR-08): keyword search; sort by price and newest; extend filters (price, category) with brand and availability where seed data supports it
- Wishlist (FR-12): save and remove favorites (local or API-backed)
- Checkout flow (FR-13–FR-15): contact + shipping address + order review; place order with confirmation screen and order number; mock payment / PaymentIntent stub acceptable
- Order history & tracking (FR-16–FR-17): list past orders; show status progression processing → shipped → delivered
- Promotions (FR-19): apply coupon code at checkout; validate against seed promos
- Support (FR-20): in-app contact/support screen with a clear contact channel
- Backend: extend NestJS OpenAPI + Prisma only as needed for orders, auth slice, coupons; keep analyze/tests green
- Baseline from prior milestones: M1 guest catalog and M2 API integration remain the foundation for Release 2 work

## Constraints
- Continue on the existing codebase—Release 2 is expansion, not a greenfield rewrite
- Demo-safe only: mock payment gateway; no real payment processor keys
- Flutter app must run on Android emulator (not a counter template app)
- flutter analyze and flutter test must pass; server tests must pass for new endpoints
- Update docs/PRD backlog section to reflect Release 2 scope; at least one QA round
- Out of scope: full admin panel (AR-01–AR-09)—document as follow-up unless time allows minimal read-only admin API
- Out of scope: production push notifications (FR-18)—log/mock only
- Out of scope: real payment processor integration

## Open questions
- Brand and store identity: official app display name, logo, primary colors, and tone of home banners—are we one vertical (e.g. general merchandise) or multi-category as seed data implies?
- Markets and compliance: which countries we ship to in the demo, currency display, and whether we need tax/VAT lines on order review for realism
- Account policy: email-only registration or phone/social login later; minimum password rules; whether guest checkout must remain after Release 2 or accounts become strongly encouraged
- Cart persistence rules: when a guest logs in, do we merge carts, replace, or ask the shopper; how long carts live on server vs device
- Wishlist: must it sync across devices for signed-in users in this release, or is device-local acceptable for demo
- Shipping: flat-rate vs tiered by order value; do we show estimated delivery dates on tracking or status labels only
- Coupons: stackable with other promos or one code per order; exclusions (sale items, categories); max discount cap
- Order tracking: carrier name and tracking number in UI or internal status only for demo
- Support channel: single channel (email form) vs phone/chat hours; SLA we promise in copy
- Password reset stub: email actually sent in demo environment or UI-only flow with message that email would be sent
- Home content: who supplies banner copy and featured product rules—manual seed, algorithm (newest), or merchandising flags in database
- Minimal read-only admin API: if attempted under time pressure, which read-only views matter most (orders list, coupon usage)
- Push notifications (FR-18 mock): which events should be logged (order shipped, back in stock) for future production scope documentation

A: Single channel for Release 2: in-app contact form that submits to a fixed support email (e.g. support@shopease-demo.com). Copy promise: “We aim to reply within one business day.” No live chat or phone line in the app—optional display of support email only, no SLA beyond that sentence.

A: Hybrid driven by seed/database: banners from seeded home content (title, image, link). Featured products use a merchandising flag on products in the database. New arrivals = rule-based (e.g. newest by created date, limited count). Categories entry from seeded category list—no manual admin UI; merchandising team sets flags and banner rows via seeds/migrations for the demo.
Q: After Release 2, must guest checkout remain fully supported with no forced account creation, or may the UX strongly encourage account creation before or after purchase while still allowing guest completion?
A: Guest checkout must remain fully supported with no forced account creation—guests can browse, cart, and complete checkout end to end. The UX may strongly encourage creating an account (e.g. banners, post-order prompt, benefits on login screen) but must never block guest completion.

Hard scope limits for this run: at most 8 user stories, at most 12 work items, at most 2 milestones, at most 12 API operations, at most 6 app screens. Cut scope to fit; keep only what the core journey needs.
Infrastructure endpoints (/health, /api/docs-json) do not count toward the API operation limit; include the health check in the contract.
These scope rules take priority over any other rule about what to include.

Rules:
- Story ids are US-001, US-002, ... Every story has at least two
  acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then form.
- Mark priority as must, should or could. Keep the first release focused:
  must-haves only cover what is needed to sell and fulfil an order.
- Include non-functional requirements (performance, security, privacy,
  accessibility, supported platforms) and an explicit out-of-scope list.

This PRD defines the scoped client-demo increment for the current run: two milestones only. M1 delivers a guest-only, Android-emulator-ready Flutter app with a cohesive design system, 12–20 locally seeded products, product list with keyword search and filters (price, category, brand, availability where seed data supports), product detail with star ratings and reviews, and an in-memory cart with quantity updates—no sign-in required for the demo meeting. Demo market for future checkout work remains United States (USD) per stakeholder clarifications.

PRD:
# ShopEase Mobile — Client Demo PRD (M1 Showable App + M2 Catalog API)

ShopEase Release 2 targets a credible mobile shopping experience (accounts, checkout, wishlist, orders, coupons, support). This PRD defines the scoped client-demo increment for the current run: two milestones only. M1 delivers a guest-only, Android-emulator-ready Flutter app with a cohesive design system, 12–20 locally seeded products, product list with keyword search and filters (price, category, brand, availability where seed data supports), product detail with star ratings and reviews, and an in-memory cart with quantity updates—no sign-in required for the demo meeting. M2 delivers a NestJS /api/v1 health check and catalog OpenAPI implementation with stub/seed data aligned to the same products; the Dart API client is generated and integrated only when flutter analyze, flutter test, and server tests pass, with M1 mock data remaining as fallback if integration blocks the demo. Prices are integer USD minor units (cents); guest checkout and full Release 2 capabilities are documented as follow-on scope. Demo market for future checkout work remains United States (USD) per stakeholder clarifications.

## Personas
### Guest Shopper (Demo Primary)
Browses without an account during the client demo; expects a polished retail app, not a template.
- Find products quickly via search and filters
- Read ratings and reviews before trusting a product
- Adjust cart quantities and see totals before a future checkout phase
- Experience smooth performance on an Android emulator

### Prospective Partner / Investor
Evaluates visual polish and whether the product feels like a real storefront backed by an API.
- See client-ready screens and consistent branding
- Understand that catalog data can come from a real backend slice
- Gain confidence the team can extend to full Release 2 without a rewrite

### Engineering / QA
Needs testable requirements, green analyze/tests, and a clear boundary between mock and API paths.
- Run flutter analyze and flutter test successfully
- Verify catalog API contracts with automated server tests
- Know acceptance criteria for M1-only vs M2-integrated builds

## User stories
### US-001 Browse seeded product catalog (must)
As a guest shopper, I want to see a scrollable list of products with image, name, and price, so that I can discover items without signing in.

- **Given** the app launches on an Android emulator with M1 mock data loaded **when** I open the primary product list screen **then** I see between 12 and 20 products each showing at least a thumbnail, display name, and price formatted as USD (e.g. $19.99) derived from integer cent amounts in data
- **Given** the product list is displayed **when** I scroll through the catalog **then** the list remains responsive without visible jank on emulator-class hardware and empty/error states show clear copy if data fails to load

### US-002 Search products by keyword (must)
As a guest shopper, I want to search the catalog by keyword, so that I can find specific items quickly.

- **Given** I am on the product list screen with the full seed catalog available **when** I enter a keyword that matches one or more product names or descriptions **then** the list updates to show only matching products and shows a no-results message when nothing matches
- **Given** I have entered a search query **when** I clear the search field **then** the full catalog list is restored

### US-003 Filter and sort catalog (must)
As a guest shopper, I want to filter by price range, category, brand, and availability and sort by price or newest, so that I can narrow choices like a real store app.

- **Given** seed data includes categories, brands, prices, and availability flags **when** I apply a category filter and a minimum/maximum price range **then** only products meeting all active filters appear in the list
- **Given** filters are applied **when** I choose sort by price (low to high or high to low) or sort by newest **then** the visible products reorder according to the selected sort without losing active filters until I reset them

### US-004 View product detail with ratings and reviews (must)
As a guest shopper, I want to open a product and see description, price, average star rating, and individual reviews, so that I can decide whether to add the item to my cart.

- **Given** I am viewing the product list **when** I tap a product **then** I navigate to a product detail screen showing name, images, price (USD from cent integers), short and long description, average star rating, and at least one seeded review with rating and text when reviews exist for that product
- **Given** I am on product detail **when** I use the system back gesture or back control **then** I return to the product list preserving my prior search/filter/sort state where technically feasible

### US-005 Manage in-memory guest cart (must)
As a guest shopper, I want to add items, change quantities, and remove lines in a cart that persists for the app session, so that I can prepare a purchase list during the demo.

- **Given** I am on product detail for an in-stock variant **when** I add a quantity to the cart **then** the cart screen shows a line with product name, unit price snapshot for display, quantity, and line subtotal in USD, and a cart badge or indicator updates on the list/detail navigation
- **Given** I have multiple cart lines **when** I increase or decrease quantity or remove a line on the cart screen **then** line subtotals and cart subtotal recalculate immediately and quantities cannot drop below 1 without removing the line or below zero

### US-006 Cohesive client-ready design system (must)
As a prospective partner viewing the demo, I want the app to use consistent typography, color, spacing, and components across catalog, detail, and cart, so that the experience reads as a intentional retail product rather than the default Flutter counter template.

- **Given** I launch the app on an Android emulator **when** I navigate among product list, product detail, and cart **then** shared components (app bar, buttons, price text, product cards) follow the same design tokens and the app does not present the stock counter demo as the main experience
- **Given** the app is built for the demo **when** engineering runs flutter analyze **then** analyze completes with no errors (warnings policy per team convention documented in README if any)

### US-007 Load catalog from NestJS OpenAPI (M2) (should)
As a guest shopper using the integrated build, I want the same catalog experience backed by /api/v1 when the API is available, so that stakeholders see API-backed retail data matching the demo products.

- **Given** M2 server is running with seeded catalog matching M1 product identities and cent-based USD prices **when** the Flutter app is configured for API mode and I open the product list **then** products load from the API with equivalent fields needed for list, search, filters, and detail including reviews where exposed by the contract
- **Given** API mode is enabled but the server is unreachable **when** I open the product list **then** the app shows a user-visible error and documented fallback behavior allows continuing on M1 local mock data without crashing

### US-008 Backend health and catalog contract tests (must)
As a QA engineer, I want a documented health endpoint and tested catalog API operations within the operation budget, so that M2 readiness is objectively verifiable before client integration.

- **Given** the NestJS application is deployed locally or in CI **when** I call GET /health (or project-standard health path) **then** I receive a success response indicating service availability and this endpoint is excluded from the 12-operation catalog budget
- **Given** catalog seed data is loaded in PostgreSQL via Prisma **when** automated server tests run for new catalog endpoints (list with query params for search/filter/sort, product by id, categories or facets as defined in OpenAPI) **then** tests pass and responses use integer minor-unit prices with currency code USD consistent with M1 mock data

## Non-functional requirements
- Platform: Flutter 3.x; primary demo target Android emulator; app must launch and complete core guest journey without sign-in.
- Quality gates: flutter test and flutter analyze pass for M1; Jest/Supertest (or project standard) pass for new M2 endpoints before Dart client generation is required.
- Money: all prices stored and transmitted as integer minor units (cents) with ISO 4217 currency USD; UI formats for display only—no floating-point currency math.
- Stock (forward-compatible): when variant stock appears in seed/API, display availability for filters; full checkout reservation rules apply in Release 2 follow-on, not this run.
- Security (M2 auth slice deferred): no production secrets in repo; JWT auth for accounts is Release 2—this run exposes only public catalog + health.
- Performance: initial catalog render within 3 seconds on emulator against local API or assets under normal dev hardware.
- Accessibility: minimum WCAG-oriented practices—semantic labels on primary actions (search, add to cart), sufficient contrast on body text and buttons, tappable targets ≥ 48dp where feasible.
- Privacy: M1 in-memory cart only—no PII collection in this increment; Release 2 will hash passwords with bcrypt or argon2 and support account deletion.
- API budget: at most 12 catalog-related operations in OpenAPI for this run; infrastructure routes (/health, /api/docs-json) do not count toward the limit.
- Screen budget: at most 6 primary app screens for this run (product list, product detail, cart, plus navigation/shell counts toward cohesive flow—no account, checkout, wishlist, or order screens in this increment).

## Out of scope
- User registration, login, logout, JWT session, and password reset (Release 2 FR-01)—guest-only for this run.
- Guest-to-signed-in cart merge, server-persisted carts, checkout, shipping address, tax lines, coupons, and mock PaymentIntent flow (Release 2 FR-02, FR-13–FR-15, FR-19).
- Home merchandising with banners, featured flags, and new-arrivals rules (Release 2 FR-03)—product list may serve as entry for this demo increment unless a dedicated home screen fits the 6-screen cap without cutting catalog quality.
- Wishlist local or API-synced (Release 2 FR-12).
- Order history, status tracking, carrier and tracking number display (Release 2 FR-16–FR-17).
- In-app support contact form (Release 2 FR-20).
- Production or live Stripe keys; real payment capture; Apple Pay / Google Pay.
- Full admin panel (AR-01–AR-09) and merchandising admin UI.
- Production push notifications (FR-18)—mock/log only in later releases.
- Production email (order confirmation, password reset delivery)—M2 may log mock confirmations only in later work.
- iOS-first polish, marketing website, multi-country shipping and VAT matrix.
- Work items requiring human approval gates, stakeholder sign-off, or style-approval waits—agents choose design tokens autonomously for the demo.

## Assumptions
- M1 ships with 12–20 products in local assets/mock JSON aligned by SKU/id with M2 database seeds.
- Single demo vertical or multi-category presentation follows seed data; no live merchandising team workflow in this run.
- Release 2 clarifications (USD, US shipping only, guest checkout remains, cart merge on login, API wishlist for signed-in users, coupon rules, flat shipping / free over $75, tracking on shipped orders, support form SLA copy, password reset UI stub, hybrid home content) apply to subsequent milestones after this catalog demo.
- Riverpod, go_router, dio, and OpenAPI-generated client are the integration path when M2 gates pass.
- If Dart client integration blocks the demo date, stakeholders accept M1 mock path with documented API readiness.
- Reviews and star ratings are seeded/static for demo credibility—not user-generated in this increment.
- Variant-level stock in seed data is simplified to product-level availability where needed to stay within API operation limits.
- OpenAPI /api/docs-json is available for client generation and does not count against the 12-operation cap.
- At most 12 engineering work items and 2 milestones (M1 showable Flutter, M2 catalog backend slice) govern delivery planning for this run.


Target stack: mobile: Flutter 3.x (Dart), Riverpod, go_router, dio, freezed/json_serializable, API client generated from OpenAPI (dart-dio); backend: NestJS (TypeScript), Prisma ORM, PostgreSQL 16, JWT auth, @nestjs/swagger; payments: Stripe (test mode); testing: flutter_test + integration_test; Jest + Supertest; delivery: Docker, docker-compose (staging), GitHub Actions; Android first
Core domain entities to consider: User, Address, Category, Product, ProductVariant, Cart, CartItem, Order, OrderItem, Payment

Reviewer feedback on the previous draft (address all of it, empty if first draft):
(none)

Scope for this run (also limits the API: only endpoints the stories need):
CLIENT DEMO (not a speed sketch). Plan exactly two milestones and build both in this run. M1 — Showable Flutter app: product list with search and filters, product detail with star ratings and reviews, in-memory cart with quantity updates, cohesive design system, 12–20 seeded products in local mock data (assets). The app must launch on an Android emulator and look client-ready (real screens, not the default Flutter counter template). Guest shopping only; no sign-in required for the demo meeting. M2 — Backend slice: NestJS /api/v1 health + catalog OpenAPI implementation with stub/seed data matching the same products; generate and integrate the Dart API client only when analyze/tests pass; if integration blocks the demo, keep M1 mock path working and document API readiness for a follow-up. Out of scope for this run: production payments, Apple/Google Pay, admin panel, marketing site, email delivery in production (mock or log order confirmation is enough for demo narrative). NEVER create work items that require human approval, stakeholder sign-off, or style-approval gates. Style tokens are chosen by agents without waiting.
Hard scope limits for this run: at most 8 user stories, at most 12 work items, at most 2 milestones, at most 12 API operations, at most 6 app screens. Cut scope to fit; keep only what the core journey needs.
Infrastructure endpoints (/health, /api/docs-json) do not count toward the API operation limit; include the health check in the contract.
These scope rules take priority over any other rule about what to include.

Deliver:
1. Components and their responsibilities.
2. Backend modules: each with its entities and the endpoints it owns.
3. Mobile app features: screens and state management per feature.
4. A complete OpenAPI 3.1 document in YAML (openapi_yaml) covering every
   endpoint the must-have stories need, with request/response schemas,
   bearer auth, pagination and a shared error schema. Every operation has
   an operationId (used to generate the mobile API client).
5. A complete Prisma schema (prisma_schema) for PostgreSQL.
6. Security design and at least three ADRs for the key decisions.

","prisma_schema":"generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

enum OrderStatus {
  pending_payment
  paid
  fulfilled
  delivered
  cancelled
  refunded
}

enum PaymentStatus {
  requires_payment_method
  requires_confirmation
  processing
  succeeded
  canceled
  failed
}

model User {
  id           String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  email        String    @unique
  passwordHash String    @map("password_hash")
  displayName  String?   @map("display_name")
  createdAt    DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt    DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  deletedAt    DateTime? @map("deleted_at")

  refreshTokens RefreshToken[]
  addresses     Address[]
  cart          Cart?
  orders        Order[]

  @@map("users")
}

model RefreshToken {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId    String   @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  tokenHash String   @map("token_hash")
  expiresAt DateTime @map("expires_at")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId])
  @@map("refresh_tokens")
}

model Address {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId     String   @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  line1      String
  line2      String?
  city       String
  state      String
  postalCode String   @map("postal_code")
  country    String   @default("US")
  isDefault  Boolean  @default(false) @map("is_default")
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId])
  @@map("addresses")
}

model Brand {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name      String
  slug      String   @unique
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  products Product[]

  @@map("brands")
}

model Category {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name      String
  slug      String   @unique
  sortOrder Int      @default(0) @map("sort_order")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  products Product[]

  @@map("categories")
}

model Product {
  id               String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name             String
  slug             String   @unique
  shortDescription String   @map("short_description")
  description      String
  brandId          String   @map("brand_id") @db.Uuid
  categoryId       String   @map("category_id") @db.Uuid
  isActive         Boolean  @default(true) @map("is_active")
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt        DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  brand    Brand            @relation(fields: [brandId], references: [id])
  category Category         @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])
  variants ProductVariant[]
  images   ProductImage[]
  reviews  Review[]

  @@index([brandId])
  @@index([categoryId])
  @@index([createdAt])
  @@map("products")
}

model ProductVariant {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId     String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  sku           String   @unique
  name          String
  priceCents    Int      @map("price_cents")
  currency      String   @default("USD")
  stockQuantity Int      @default(0) @map("stock_quantity")
  isDefault     Boolean  @default(false) @map("is_default")
  isActive      Boolean  @default(true) @map("is_active")
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  product Product        @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  images  ProductImage[]

  @@index([productId])
  @@map("product_variants")
}

model ProductImage {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  variantId String?  @map("variant_id") @db.Uuid
  url       String
  sortOrder Int      @default(0) @map("sort_order")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  product Product         @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  variant ProductVariant? @relation(fields: [variantId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@index([productId])
  @@map("product_images")
}

model Review {
  id                  String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId           String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  rating              Int
  title               String
  body                String
  reviewerDisplayName String   @map("reviewer_display_name")
  createdAt           DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt           DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  product Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([productId])
  @@map("reviews")
}

model Cart {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId    String   @unique @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user  User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  items CartItem[]

  @@map("carts")
}

model CartItem {
  id               String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  cartId           String   @map("cart_id") @db.Uuid
  productVariantId String   @map("product_variant_id") @db.Uuid
  quantity         Int
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt        DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  cart Cart @relation(fields: [cartId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([cartId, productVariantId])
  @@map("cart_items")
}

model Order {
  id              String      @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId          String      @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  status          OrderStatus @default(pending_payment)
  currency        String      @default("USD")
  subtotalCents   Int         @map("subtotal_cents")
  shippingCents   Int         @default(0) @map("shipping_cents")
  taxCents        Int         @default(0) @map("tax_cents")
  totalCents      Int         @map("total_cents")
  createdAt       DateTime    @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt       DateTime    @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user     User        @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  items    OrderItem[]
  payments Payment[]

  @@index([userId])
  @@index([status])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderItem {
  id               String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  orderId          String   @map("order_id") @db.Uuid
  productVariantId String?  @map("product_variant_id") @db.Uuid
  productName      String   @map("product_name")
  variantName      String   @map("variant_name")
  sku              String
  unitPriceCents   Int      @map("unit_price_cents")
  currency         String   @default("USD")
  quantity         Int
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt        DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  order Order @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([orderId])
  @@map("order_items")
}

model Payment {
  id                    String        @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  orderId               String        @map("order_id") @db.Uuid
  stripePaymentIntentId String        @unique @map("stripe_payment_intent_id")
  status                PaymentStatus
  amountCents           Int           @map("amount_cents")
  currency              String        @default("USD")
  createdAt             DateTime      @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt             DateTime      @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  order Order @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([orderId])
  @@map("payments")
}
"}

Format as $X.YY only in Flutter presentation layer.","consequences":"All filters (minPriceCents/maxPriceCents) and cart math use integer arithmetic; OpenAPI Money schema is reused everywhere for consistency with Release 2 checkout."},{"id":"ADR-003","title":"OpenAPI contract-first with operationId-driven dart-dio client","context":"Team convention: no hand-written HTTP endpoints in Flutter; NestJS must match the published contract.","decision":"Author complete OpenAPI 3.1 under docs/openapi.yaml first; generate packages/api_client after M2 Supertest/Jest pass; Nest controllers and DTOs conform to the same schemas.","consequences":"Breaking API changes require spec bump and regen; operationIds (getHealth, listProducts, getProductById, listProductReviews, listCategories, listBrands) are stable client method names."},{"id":"ADR-004","title":"Guest in-memory cart only for M1/M2","context":"Signed-in carts, checkout, and stock reservation are Release 2; demo needs cart badge and totals without backend cart APIs.","decision":"Cart state lives in a Riverpod CartNotifier for the app session only; add-to-cart uses default variant from detail; unit price snapshot stored on each line for display.","consequences":"No cart sync across devices; merging on login is deferred. Stock is not decremented on add-to-cart until Release 2 checkout reservation."},{"id":"ADR-005","title":"Catalog API bounded to five read operations plus health","context":"PRD caps catalog-related OpenAPI operations at 12; infrastructure routes excluded.","decision":"Ship list products (with search/filter/sort), get product, list reviews, list categories, list brands—five catalog operations. Embed averageRating and reviewCount on list/detail responses to avoid extra aggregate endpoints.","consequences":"Filter UI loads categories/brands once; heavy review lists paginate on GET .../reviews. Room remains under the 12-op cap for minor additions without scope creep."}],"openapi_yaml":"openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: ShopEase Mobile API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: |
    ShopEase Client Demo (M1 Flutter + M2 catalog slice). Public catalog and health
    for guest demo. Auth, cart, orders, and payments are Release 2.
    Prices are integer USD cents with ISO 4217 currency code USD.
  contact:
    name: ShopEase Engineering
jsonSchemaDialect: https://spec.openapis.org/oas/3.1/dialect/base
servers:
  - url: http://10.0.2.2:3000/api/v1
    description: Android emulator to local NestJS
  - url: http://localhost:3000/api/v1
    description: Local development
  - url: https://api.staging.shopease.example/api/v1
    description: Staging
tags:
  - name: Health
    description: Service availability (not counted in catalog operation budget)
  - name: Catalog
    description: Public product browse, facets, and reviews
paths:
  /health:
    get:
      tags:
        - Health
      operationId: getHealth
      summary: Health check
      description: Returns 200 when the service and database are reachable.
      security: []
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Service is healthy
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/HealthResponse'
        '503':
          description: Service unavailable
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse'
  /products:
    get:
      tags:
        - Catalog
      operationId: listProducts
      summary: List products
      description: |
        Paginated catalog with keyword search, filters (category, brand, price range,
        availability), and sort. Supports US-001, US-002, US-003.
      security: []
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Page'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PageSize'
        - name: q
          in: query
          description: Case-insensitive search in product name, brand name, and description
          schema:
            type: string
            maxLength: 120
        - name: categorySlug
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            maxLength: 64
        - name: brandSlug
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            maxLength: 64
        - name: minPriceCents
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            minimum: 0
        - name: maxPriceCents
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            minimum: 0
        - name: inStock
          in: query
          description: When true, only products with at least one in-stock variant
          schema:
            type: boolean
        - name: sort
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            enum:
              - newest
              - priceAsc
              - priceDesc
            default: newest
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Paginated product summaries
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ProductListResponse'
        '400':
          description: Invalid query parameters
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse'
  /products/{productId}:
    get:
      tags:
        - Catalog
      operationId: getProductById
      summary: Get product detail
      description: Full product with variants, rating summary, and image URLs. US-004.
      security: []
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ProductId'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Product detail
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ProductDetail'
        '404':
          description: Product not found
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse'
  /products/{productId}/reviews:
    get:
      tags:
        - Catalog
      operationId: listProductReviews
      summary: List product reviews
      description: Paginated seeded reviews for product detail. US-004.
      security: []
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ProductId'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Page'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PageSize'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Paginated reviews
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ReviewListResponse'
        '404':
          description: Product not found
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse'
  /categories:
    get:
      tags:
        - Catalog
      operationId: listCategories
      summary: List categories
      description: Facet list for filter UI (US-003).
      security: []
      responses:
        '200':
          description: All active categories
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/CategoryListResponse'
        '500':
          description: Internal server error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse'
  /brands:
    get:
      tags:
        - Catalog
      operationId: listBrands
      summary: List brands
      description: Facet list for filter UI (US-003).
      security: []
      responses:
        '200':
          description: All active brands
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/BrandListResponse'
        '500':
          description: Internal server error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse'
components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth:

      scheme: bearer

      description: |
        JWT access token (15 min TTL). Required for Release 2 protected resources.
        All operations in this document use security [] unless extended later.
  parameters:
    Page:
      name: page
      in: query
      schema:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        default: 1
    PageSize:
      name: pageSize
      in: query
      schema:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        maximum: 100
        default: 20
    ProductId:

        type: string

  schemas:
    HealthResponse:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required:
        - status
        - database
        - timestamp

          type: string
          enum: [ok, degraded]
        database:
          type: string
          enum: [up, down]
        timestamp:
          type: string
          format: date-time
    ErrorResponse:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required:
        - statusCode
        - error

          example: 400

            - type: array

                type: string
    Money:

      properties:

          type: number

          type: integer

    Category:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required:
        - id
        - name
        - slug
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid

    Brand:

      additionalProperties: false

        - id

          type: string

          type: string
    ProductSummary:

        price:

          type: string

    ProductListResponse:

    ProductVariant:

      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        sku:
          type: string
        name:
          type: string
        price:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Money'
        stockQuantity:
          type: integer
          minimum: 0
        imageUrl:
          type: string
          format: uri
        isDefault:
          type: boolean
    ProductDetail:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required:
        - id
        - name
        - brand
        - shortDescription
        - description
        - category
        - price
        - primaryImageUrl
        - imageUrls
        - inStock
        - rating
        - variants
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        name:
          type: string

          type: string
        shortDescription:
          type: string
        description:

        price:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Money'
        primaryImageUrl:

","prisma_schema":"generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

enum OrderStatus {
  pending_payment
  paid
  fulfilled
  delivered
  cancelled
  refunded
}

enum PaymentStatus {
  requires_payment_method
  requires_confirmation
  processing
  succeeded
  canceled
  failed
}

model User {
  id           String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  email        String    @unique
  passwordHash String    @map("password_hash")
  displayName  String?   @map("display_name")
  createdAt    DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt    DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  deletedAt    DateTime? @map("deleted_at")

  refreshTokens RefreshToken[]
  addresses     Address[]
  cart          Cart?
  orders        Order[]

  @@map("users")
}

model RefreshToken {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId    String   @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  tokenHash String   @map("token_hash")
  expiresAt DateTime @map("expires_at")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId])
  @@map("refresh_tokens")
}

model Address {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId     String   @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  line1      String
  line2      String?
  city       String
  state      String
  postalCode String   @map("postal_code")
  country    String   @default("US")
  isDefault  Boolean  @default(false) @map("is_default")
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId])
  @@map("addresses")
}

model Brand {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name      String
  slug      String   @unique
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  products Product[]

  @@map("brands")
}

model Category {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name      String
  slug      String   @unique
  sortOrder Int      @default(0) @map("sort_order")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  products Product[]

  @@map("categories")
}

model Product {
  id               String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name             String
  slug             String   @unique
  shortDescription String   @map("short_description")
  description      String
  brandId          String   @map("brand_id") @db.Uuid
  categoryId       String   @map("category_id") @db.Uuid
  isActive         Boolean  @default(true) @map("is_active")
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt        DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  brand    Brand            @relation(fields: [brandId], references: [id])
  category Category         @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])
  variants ProductVariant[]
  images   ProductImage[]
  reviews  Review[]

  @@index([brandId])
  @@index([categoryId])
  @@index([createdAt])
  @@map("products")
}

model ProductVariant {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId     String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  sku           String   @unique
  name          String
  priceCents    Int      @map("price_cents")
  currency      String   @default("USD")
  stockQuantity Int      @default(0) @map("stock_quantity")
  isDefault     Boolean  @default(false) @map("is_default")
  isActive      Boolean  @default(true) @map("is_active")
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  product Product        @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  images  ProductImage[]

  @@index([productId])
  @@map("product_variants")
}

model ProductImage {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  variantId String?  @map("variant_id") @db.Uuid
  url       String
  sortOrder Int      @default(0) @map("sort_order")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  product Product         @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  variant ProductVariant? @relation(fields: [variantId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@index([productId])
  @@map("product_images")
}

model Review {
  id                  String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId           String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  rating              Int
  title               String
  body                String
  reviewerDisplayName String   @map("reviewer_display_name")
  createdAt           DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt           DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  product Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([productId])
  @@map("reviews")
}

model Cart {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId    String   @unique @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user  User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  items CartItem[]

  @@map("carts")
}

model CartItem {
  id               String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  cartId           String   @map("cart_id") @db.Uuid
  productVariantId String   @map("product_variant_id") @db.Uuid
  quantity         Int
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt        DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  cart Cart @relation(fields: [cartId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([cartId, productVariantId])
  @@map("cart_items")
}

model Order {
  id              String      @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId          String      @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  status          OrderStatus @default(pending_payment)
  currency        String      @default("USD")
  subtotalCents   Int         @map("subtotal_cents")
  shippingCents   Int         @default(0) @map("shipping_cents")
  taxCents        Int         @default(0) @map("tax_cents")
  totalCents      Int         @map("total_cents")
  createdAt       DateTime    @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt       DateTime    @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user     User        @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  items    OrderItem[]
  payments Payment[]

  @@index([userId])
  @@index([status])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderItem {
  id               String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  orderId          String   @map("order_id") @db.Uuid
  productVariantId String?  @map("product_variant_id") @db.Uuid
  productName      String   @map("product_name")
  variantName      String   @map("variant_name")
  sku              String
  unitPriceCents   Int      @map("unit_price_cents")
  currency         String   @default("USD")
  quantity         Int
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt        DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  order Order @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([orderId])
  @@map("order_items")
}

model Payment {
  id                    String        @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  orderId               String        @map("order_id") @db.Uuid
  stripePaymentIntentId String        @unique @map("stripe_payment_intent_id")
  status                PaymentStatus
  amountCents           Int           @map("amount_cents")
  currency              String        @default("USD")
  createdAt             DateTime      @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt             DateTime      @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  order Order @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([orderId])
  @@map("payments")
}
"}

structured_output.overview: ShopEase Mobile Client Demo (M1 + M2) delivers a guest-only, Android-emulator-ready Flutter retail experience backed optionally by a NestJS catalog slice. M1 ships 12–20 locally seeded products (assets/mock JSON), cohesive design tokens, product list with keyword search and filters (price, category, brand, availability), product detail with average star rating and seeded reviews, and a session-scoped in-memory cart—no authentication. M2 adds PostgreSQL + Prisma seed data aligned to the same product identities (SKUs/UUIDs), GET /api/v1/health, and a contract-first OpenAPI 3.1 catalog API (≤12 catalog operations; /health and /api/docs-json excluded from the budget). The Flutter app uses a CatalogRepository abstraction: default mock (M1), optional API mode via generated dart-dio client when server tests pass; unreachable API shows error with documented fallback to mock. Release 2 entities (User, Cart persistence, Orders, Stripe) are modeled in Prisma and declared in OpenAPI security but have no endpoints in this increment. Global API prefix /api/v1; money is integer USD cents everywhere; variant-level stock in data with product-level inStock for filters.

components.name: Flutter Mobile App (shopease_app)
components.responsibility: Guest catalog browse, search/filter/sort UI, product detail with reviews, in-memory cart, design system, loading/empty/error states, optional API-backed catalog via generated client and mock fallback.
components.technology: Flutter 3.x, Riverpod (AsyncNotifier), go_router, flutter_secure_storage (reserved for R2), packages/api_client (OpenAPI dart-dio), integration_test for critical journeys.

components.name: NestJS API Server
components.responsibility: Public health probe and catalog read API matching OpenAPI; thin controllers, catalog/health services, Prisma persistence, class-validator DTOs, Swagger from contract.

components.name: PostgreSQL Database
components.responsibility: Persist seeded catalog (brands, categories, products, variants, images, reviews) for M2; schema includes forward-compatible commerce tables unused until Release 2.

components.name: OpenAPI Contract (docs/openapi.yaml)
components.responsibility: Single source of truth for request/response shapes, operationIds for client generation, shared ErrorResponse and pagination patterns.
components.technology: OpenAPI 3.1 YAML; NestJS implements to match; CI verifies Supertest against spec.

components.name: Prisma ORM Layer
components.responsibility: Type-safe data access, migrations, seed script for 12–20 demo products mirroring M1 mock JSON.

components.name: Docker Compose (staging)
components.responsibility: Local PostgreSQL + API container for emulator (host 10.0.2.2:3000) and CI e2e.

components.name: M1 Local Mock Catalog
components.responsibility: Identical field shapes to API ProductSummary/ProductDetail for offline demo and API-failure fallback.
components.technology: JSON in assets/, CatalogRepository mock implementation.

backend_modules.name: health
backend_modules.responsibility: Liveness and database connectivity for ops and US-008; excluded from catalog operation budget.

backend_modules.name: catalog
backend_modules.responsibility: Public read-only catalog: paginated product list with search, filters, sort; product detail; product reviews; facet lists for categories and brands.

backend_modules.name: auth
backend_modules.responsibility: JWT access/refresh (Release 2 FR-01); no routes exposed in M1/M2 increment.

backend_modules.name: users
backend_modules.responsibility: Profiles, addresses, account deletion (Release 2); not implemented this run.

backend_modules.name: cart
backend_modules.responsibility: Server-persisted carts for signed-in users (Release 2); M1 cart is client-only.

backend_modules.name: orders
backend_modules.responsibility: Order lifecycle pending_payment → paid → fulfilled → delivered (+ cancelled/refunded) with immutable line snapshots (Release 2).

backend_modules.name: payments
backend_modules.responsibility: Stripe PaymentIntent creation and webhook handling (Release 2 test mode).

app_features.name: core

app_features.state_management: AppConfigNotifier (API base URL, catalog source enum mock|api); ThemeMode; go_router routes; Dio + generated ApiClient wrapper with interceptors (no auth header in M2).

app_features.name: catalog
screens: ProductListScreen (search bar, filter/sort chips, infinite scroll or paged list)
ProductDetailScreen (gallery, price, rating, reviews section, add-to-cart)
CatalogFilterSheet (modal: price range, category, brand, in-stock only)
app_features.state_management: ProductListNotifier (AsyncNotifier): query q, categorySlug, brandSlug, min/max price cents, inStock, sort, page; preserves state on back from detail. ProductDetailNotifier: load by productId. CategoriesProvider / BrandsProvider: cache facet lists from API or mock.

app_features.name: cart
screens: CartScreen (line items, qty steppers, remove, subtotal)
app_features.state_management: CartNotifier (Notifier): Map keyed by variantId with product name and unit price snapshot (cents), quantity rules (min 1 or remove); CartBadge derived from total item count; no persistence beyond app session.

structured_output.data_model_notes: Money is stored on ProductVariant as priceCents (Int) and currency (String, default USD). Product list display price is the default variant’s price; inStock is true when any active variant has stockQuantity > 0 (simplified product-level availability for filters). Reviews are seeded static rows (reviewerDisplayName only, no user FK in M2). Product and variant SKUs align between assets/mock JSON and prisma/seed.ts. OrderItem and cart lines in Release 2 will snapshot name and unitPriceCents at purchase time. Images: ProductImage with sortOrder; primaryImageUrl in API is first image or variant default. Categories and brands use stable slug filters in query params. UUIDs for all public IDs. Indexes on product (categoryId, brandId, createdAt), variant (productId), review (productId), and full-text or ILIKE search on name/description implemented in service layer for M2.
security: M2 exposes only unauthenticated read endpoints for health and catalog; no PII collected in the demo increment.
Bearer JWT securityScheme is declared in OpenAPI for Release 2 protected routes; catalog operations explicitly set security: [] so generated clients do not require tokens in M2.
Secrets (DATABASE_URL, future JWT secrets, Stripe keys) via environment variables validated at Nest startup; never committed.
Passwords in Release 2: bcrypt or argon2; support account deletion per domain rules.
Mobile: release builds HTTPS-only; debug Android network security config allows cleartext only to 10.0.2.2 for local API.
Card data never touches our server in Release 2 (Stripe SDK + webhooks).
Input validation on all query DTOs (page, pageSize caps, price bounds) to reduce abuse; rate limiting recommended before production.
CORS restricted to known app origins in staging/production; permissive localhost for dev.

adrs.title: M1 mock catalog with optional M2 API mode and mock fallback
adrs.context: Client demo date is fixed; M2 integration depends on green server tests and Dart client generation. Stakeholders still need a showable app if the API slips.
adrs.decision: Implement CatalogRepository with two backends (LocalMockCatalogRepository, ApiCatalogRepository). Default to mock; enable API via build flag or runtime config after tests pass. On API errors, show user-visible error and allow continuing on mock data without crashing.
adrs.consequences: Slightly more abstraction in Flutter, but demo risk is low and US-007 acceptance is met. Engineers must keep mock JSON and Prisma seed in sync by shared SKU/id manifest.

adrs.title: Integer minor-unit money (USD cents) end-to-end
adrs.context: Floating-point currency causes rounding bugs; PRD and ecommerce domain rules require ISO 4217 codes and integer minor units.
adrs.decision: Store priceCents as Int and currency as String (USD) in PostgreSQL, API JSON, and mock data. Format as $X.YY only in Flutter presentation layer.
adrs.consequences: All filters (minPriceCents/maxPriceCents) and cart math use integer arithmetic; OpenAPI Money schema is reused everywhere for consistency with Release 2 checkout.

adrs.title: OpenAPI contract-first with operationId-driven dart-dio client
adrs.context: Team convention: no hand-written HTTP endpoints in Flutter; NestJS must match the published contract.
adrs.decision: Author complete OpenAPI 3.1 under docs/openapi.yaml first; generate packages/api_client after M2 Supertest/Jest pass; Nest controllers and DTOs conform to the same schemas.
adrs.consequences: Breaking API changes require spec bump and regen; operationIds (getHealth, listProducts, getProductById, listProductReviews, listCategories, listBrands) are stable client method names.

adrs.title: Guest in-memory cart only for M1/M2
adrs.context: Signed-in carts, checkout, and stock reservation are Release 2; demo needs cart badge and totals without backend cart APIs.
adrs.decision: Cart state lives in a Riverpod CartNotifier for the app session only; add-to-cart uses default variant from detail; unit price snapshot stored on each line for display.
adrs.consequences: No cart sync across devices; merging on login is deferred. Stock is not decremented on add-to-cart until Release 2 checkout reservation.

adrs.title: Catalog API bounded to five read operations plus health
adrs.context: PRD caps catalog-related OpenAPI operations at 12; infrastructure routes excluded.
adrs.decision: Ship list products (with search/filter/sort), get product, list reviews, list categories, list brands—five catalog operations. Embed averageRating and reviewCount on list/detail responses to avoid extra aggregate endpoints.
adrs.consequences: Filter UI loads categories/brands once; heavy review lists paginate on GET .../reviews. Room remains under the 12-op cap for minor additions without scope creep.

structured_output.prisma_schema:
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

enum OrderStatus {
  pending_payment
  paid
  fulfilled
  delivered
  cancelled
  refunded
}

enum PaymentStatus {
  requires_payment_method
  requires_confirmation
  processing
  succeeded
  canceled
  failed
}

model User {
  id           String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  email        String    @unique
  passwordHash String    @map("password_hash")
  displayName  String?   @map("display_name")
  createdAt    DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt    DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  deletedAt    DateTime? @map("deleted_at")

  refreshTokens RefreshToken[]
  addresses     Address[]
  cart          Cart?
  orders        Order[]

  @@map("users")
}

model RefreshToken {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId    String   @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  tokenHash String   @map("token_hash")
  expiresAt DateTime @map("expires_at")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId])
  @@map("refresh_tokens")
}

model Address {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId     String   @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  line1      String
  line2      String?
  city       String
  state      String
  postalCode String   @map("postal_code")
  country    String   @default("US")
  isDefault  Boolean  @default(false) @map("is_default")
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId])
  @@map("addresses")
}

model Brand {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name      String
  slug      String   @unique
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  products Product[]

  @@map("brands")
}

model Category {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name      String
  slug      String   @unique
  sortOrder Int      @default(0) @map("sort_order")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  products Product[]

  @@map("categories")
}

model Product {
  id               String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name             String
  slug             String   @unique
  shortDescription String   @map("short_description")
  description      String
  brandId          String   @map("brand_id") @db.Uuid
  categoryId       String   @map("category_id") @db.Uuid
  isActive         Boolean  @default(true) @map("is_active")
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt        DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  brand    Brand            @relation(fields: [brandId], references: [id])
  category Category         @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])
  variants ProductVariant[]
  images   ProductImage[]
  reviews  Review[]

  @@index([brandId])
  @@index([categoryId])
  @@index([createdAt])
  @@map("products")
}

model ProductVariant {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId     String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  sku           String   @unique
  name          String
  priceCents    Int      @map("price_cents")
  currency      String   @default("USD")
  stockQuantity Int      @default(0) @map("stock_quantity")
  isDefault     Boolean  @default(false) @map("is_default")
  isActive      Boolean  @default(true) @map("is_active")
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  product Product        @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  images  ProductImage[]

  @@index([productId])
  @@map("product_variants")
}

model ProductImage {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  variantId String?  @map("variant_id") @db.Uuid
  url       String
  sortOrder Int      @default(0) @map("sort_order")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  product Product         @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  variant ProductVariant? @relation(fields: [variantId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@index([productId])
  @@map("product_images")
}

model Review {
  id                  String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  productId           String   @map("product_id") @db.Uuid
  rating              Int
  title               String
  body                String
  reviewerDisplayName String   @map("reviewer_display_name")
  createdAt           DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt           DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  product Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([productId])
  @@map("reviews")
}

model Cart {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId    String   @unique @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user  User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  items CartItem[]

  @@map("carts")
}

model CartItem {
  id               String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  cartId           String   @map("cart_id") @db.Uuid
  productVariantId String   @map("product_variant_id") @db.Uuid
  quantity         Int
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt        DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  cart Cart @relation(fields: [cartId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([cartId, productVariantId])
  @@map("cart_items")
}

model Order {
  id              String      @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId          String      @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  status          OrderStatus @default(pending_payment)
  currency        String      @default("USD")
  subtotalCents   Int         @map("subtotal_cents")
  shippingCents   Int         @default(0) @map("shipping_cents")
  taxCents        Int         @default(0) @map("tax_cents")
  totalCents      Int         @map("total_cents")
  createdAt       DateTime    @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt       DateTime    @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user     User        @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  items    OrderItem[]
  payments Payment[]

  @@index([userId])
  @@index([status])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderItem {
  id               String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  orderId          String   @map("order_id") @db.Uuid
  productVariantId String?  @map("product_variant_id") @db.Uuid
  productName      String   @map("product_name")
  variantName      String   @map("variant_name")
  sku              String
  unitPriceCents   Int      @map("unit_price_cents")
  currency         String   @default("USD")
  quantity         Int
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt        DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  order Order @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([orderId])
  @@map("order_items")
}

model Payment {
  id                    String        @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  orderId               String        @map("order_id") @db.Uuid
  stripePaymentIntentId String        @unique @map("stripe_payment_intent_id")
  status                PaymentStatus
  amountCents           Int           @map("amount_cents")
  currency              String        @default("USD")
  createdAt             DateTime      @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt             DateTime      @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  order Order @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([orderId])
  @@map("payments")
}
